title: Nine-Tooth Route Rasterization
question: Follow the connected route from the amber triangle to the teal circle. It has nine V-shaped teeth. In route order, write a dark cell for a tooth pointing up and a light cell for a tooth pointing down, filling a 3 by 3 tile left-to-right and top-to-bottom. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

task_signature.mechanism: Traverse one connected route, decode each tooth's vertical sign, and rasterize the ordered signs into a 3 by 3 symbol.

latent_z.description: A balanced glyph bit string and independently varied local placement, scale, stroke, direction, ink palette, background, and harmless remote decorations.

latent_alias.justification: The rendered route directly exposes every label-bearing tooth sign; no nontrivial render-invariant relabeling is present in this minimal scene representation.

boundary.observable: The amber triangular cap fixes the route start, the teal round cap fixes its end, and all nine V-shaped teeth are visibly joined by one uninterrupted dark stroke.
boundary.quarantine: The sampler uses wide teeth and fixed sign clearance; malformed, interrupted, or ambiguously decoded routes make the pixel inverse abstain.

semantic_contrast.contrast: Unlike winding-filmstrip rectification, there are no sampled cross-sections to rotate; unlike toggle-route reveal, there are no colored commands or evolving state; unlike odd-vertex reassembly, no vertices are discarded or reconnected. The geometry of each successive tooth is itself one binary sample, and the declared transform serializes those signed samples into a raster.
semantic_contrast.expected_information_gain: It isolates whether a model can preserve start-directed order along one compact connected trace while converting local geometric signs into a two-dimensional raster symbol.
